abstract: Evaluates facility substructure stability and hydrologic inundation clearances
system_message:
You are the Structural and geological survey lead (STRUCT), responsible for evaluating facility substructure stability and hydrologic inundation clearances as well as conducting seismic damping surveys across candidate emergency repository facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Seismic damping survey（SEIS）
information_points.content:
STRUCT-SEIS-FZU：According to the geotechnical seismic assessment log, St. Jude Subterranean Vault has a foundation seismic acceleration rating of 0.25 g, representing the peak horizontal ground acceleration sustained at the subterranean bedrock foundation anchor points without structural distortion.
STRUCT-SEIS-E0E：According to the geotechnical seismic assessment log, Highland Quarry Underground Complex has a foundation seismic acceleration rating of 0.45 g, reflecting the peak horizontal ground acceleration sustained at the subterranean bedrock foundation anchor points without structural distortion.
STRUCT-SEIS-MS0：According to the geotechnical seismic assessment log, Blackwood Ridge Secure Archive has a foundation seismic acceleration rating of 0.35 g, representing the peak horizontal ground acceleration sustained at subterranean bedrock foundation anchor points without structural distortion.

information_points.title: Evaluates facility substructure stability and hydrologic inundation clearances（HYDRO）
information_points.content:
STRUCT-HYDRO-WUX：For Highland Quarry Underground Complex, the hydraulic inundation modeling report records an elevation above base flood level of 6.2 m, measured as the vertical clearance between the regional 500-year base flood elevation and the lowest subterranean entry threshold and exhaust plenum.
STRUCT-HYDRO-E0Y：For Blackwood Ridge Secure Archive, the hydraulic inundation modeling report indicates an elevation above base flood level of 1.8 m, measured as the vertical clearance from the regional 500-year base flood elevation to the lowest subterranean entry threshold and exhaust plenum.
STRUCT-HYDRO-LJF：For St. Jude Subterranean Vault, the hydraulic inundation modeling report shows an elevation above base flood level of 6.2 m, measured as the vertical clearance between the regional 500-year base flood elevation and the lowest subterranean entry threshold and exhaust plenum.
